If you think you or someone else is in immediate risk of injury, call 999 and ask for the police.

What is serious abuse at work

You’re being seriously abused or exploited at work if you believe you’re being controlled, threatened or manipulated. This could be an indicator of modern slavery.

Signs of abuse or exploitation can include:

being threatened with violence or harm

not being allowed to leave your workplace or accommodation

not being allowed to speak to other people

having your passport taken away

not being allowed to get medical treatment

being forced to live in accommodation provided by your employer

being made to stay in unsafe or unsuitable accommodation

having your wages withheld or being forced to give wages back to your employer

being forced to work to pay off a debt that keeps increasing

If this does not describe your situation

You can report other problems at work, such as pay, workplace disputes and immigration issues.

Report serious abuse online

Use the online form to tell us if you think you or someone else is being abused or exploited.

We will not share your details with anyone you tell us about in your report.

Start now

Other ways to report

By email

contact@fairworkagency.gov.uk

Try to include:

what the abuse is

where it’s happening, or happened

any relevant pictures or documents

your name and contact details – we’ll only use these to ask you questions about your report, if needed

By phone

0800 432 0804.

Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm (except public holidays). You can still call outside of these hours and leave a voice message.

Calls are free.

We can arrange for an interpreter, if needed

Who investigates your report

If you work in England or Wales

The Fair Work Agency will investigate your report.

If you work in Scotland or Northern Ireland

The Fair Work Agency will investigate your report if you work in:

agriculture

horticulture

shellfish gathering

food processing and packaging

For all other sectors:

Police Scotland will investigate reports from workers in Scotland.

The Police Service of Northern Ireland will investigate reports from workers in Northern Ireland.

You do not need to work out who should deal with your report. We will send it to the right organisation.

How to report other problems at work

Problems with pay

Use the complain about pay and work rights form if the problem is about:

being forced to work more than 48 hours per week

not being paid National Minimum wage

not being paid by an employment agency

Contact the HMRC Statutory Pay Dispute Team if the problem is about:

holiday pay

sick pay

maternity pay

paternity pay

Bullying, harassment or workplace disputes

Contact Acas for free advice and support about:

bullying or harassment at work

unfair dismissal

workplace disputes

poor management practices

disciplinary or grievance issues

Immigration issues

Use the report an Immigration or Border Crime form if the problem is about:

a Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS)

someone working in the UK illegally

illegal immigration or smuggling
